source.citation: Chicagology, “Calumet Club” (Golden Age page 063) — a compilation reprinting the Chicago Tribune's reporting of the Calumet Club's annual receptions to the Old Settlers of Chicago, with the club's own building descriptions.

transcribes.note: The forty names this project reads as the death roll.
transcribes.work: Chicago Tribune, “THE OLD SETTLERS. Deaths During the Year.” — the fourth annual reception announced for 18 May, and John Wentworth's list of old settlers dead since 1 January 1881

transcribes.note: The Mansion House at 50 cents for a blanket, the North Side's few white wooden houses and one brick-and-stone building, Kinzie's white house by Clark street bridge, no buildings on the south bank until Dearborn street, and the Indian camps — all of 1832, three years before the scene.
transcribes.work: Chicago Tribune, interview with Capt. Thomas S. Eells of Jacksonville, Fla., who came to Chicago in 1832 with Gurdon S. Hubbard

transcribes.note: The roster this pass read: 128 printed entries against the report's own count of 118 guests in the house, 414 known old settlers, 35 deaths in the year, 160 guests at the third reception.
transcribes.work: Chicago Tribune, report of the Calumet Club's fourth annual reception to the Old Settlers of Chicago, with the list “Names of Old Settlers Present, Residents and of Age Prior to 1840” and the speeches of Vice-President J. W. Doane and the Hon. John Wentworth

transcribes.note: Used for one fact only: that the club, organised in 1878, “occupied for the first few years of its existence the residence of the late General Anson Stager, at the corner of Michigan Avenue and Eighteenth Street” — which is where the receptions of 1879-1882 were held.
transcribes.work: The Chicago Clubs Illustrated (Chicago: Lanward Publishing Company)

what_it_does_not_supply: any year of arrival for the 1882 guests — the roster gives each guest's 1882 post-office address and no arrival date
any 1835 residence: the addresses printed are where these men lived in 1882, forty-seven years after the scene date
an 1835 resident. The club's criterion reaches to 31 December 1839, so a name on this page cannot by itself put anyone in the town on 1 July 1835
what_it_supplies: the names on two 1882 rolls of Chicago's pre-1840 settlers, and the club's criterion for being on them
the reception SERIES: which reception was which, how many attended, and how many had died
Eells's 1832 description of the town, which is a townscape claim three years early
